executive_assessment.text: Khanfar/Wadi Bana adds a concrete multi-driver water-allocation case; rainfall, war damage, diversion and governance must be read together, not as a single climate cause.
Al-Malakha's women-led mediation provides a historical capacity example, while Hodeidah, Shibam and Hadramaut activities are reported outputs or participant accounts.
Evaluation-summary findings caution that short timeframes, coherence and ownership constrain sustainability despite promising water-user capacities.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-12 reports: In Khanfar, climate-change-related rainfall shifts reportedly reduced Wadi Bana flow and irrigation; conflict had damaged or destroyed 85% of irrigation infrastructure by late 2023. Some farmers diverted water from downstream users, who feared violence.

Source dated 2024-12 reports: In Al-Malakha, a dam serving about 350 farmers had been a violent conflict flashpoint. A women’s unit in the local WUA helped negotiate permitted shallow wells and a pipeline; the approach was replicated in 14 other villages with armed conflict.

Source dated 2024-03-01 reports: In Al-Sukhnah and Al-Mansouriyah, Hodeidah, UNDP reports floods and heatwaves damaging farmland and crops; SFD reported 379 spillways across the districts, nearly 100 hectares benefited by reservoirs and 299 hectares protected by spillways.

Source dated 2024-03-01 reports: A named farmer in Sanif Al-Monasarah, Al-Mansouriyah, said spillways prevented soil erosion and helped restore irrigation; a project account says the work enabled her to return to crop production after land degradation had stopped cultivation.

Source dated 2026-02-05 reports: In Wadi Bin Ali, Shibam, a farmer reported leaving fields uncultivated for months because seasonal spate irrigation, damaged canals and poor floodwater retention constrained production; beekeeping supplemented income.
FAO's February 2026 Shibam feature reports greenhouse distribution and cash-for-work, with 102 facilities targeted for rehabilitation and participant accounts of more regular production.

Source dated 2025-04-24 reports: For flood-prone Mukalla and Seiyun, SIERY equipped local authorities to manage flood waste, improve drainage and rehabilitate rural roads; in Hadramaut, the project also rehabilitated irrigation canals for local agriculture.

known_gaps.text: Localized climate, aquifer, groundwater-recharge, rainfall-intensity, coastal, and settlement exposure evidence is incomplete because observation systems are degraded and national projections have wide local uncertainty.

Current evidence from de facto authority areas, inaccessible districts, women, displaced people, persons with disabilities, pastoralists, and remote communities is uneven and often not comparable across territories.
Independent evaluations document delivery and implementation constraints but rarely establish durable maintenance, welfare, aquifer, livelihood, inclusion, climate-resilience, or peace outcomes.
The fcv-to-climate pathway is directly supported at system level, but quantitative estimates of conflict's additional effect on hazard losses, adaptation costs, and recovery duration are absent.
Water-dispute and mobility pathways remain conditional and local; stronger event-specific, longitudinal, and counterfactual evidence is needed before making national climate-conflict claims.
The FAO resilience evaluation report link returned HTTP 403; one claim is limited to the explicit publisher-page summary and has no local breakdown.
A 2024 UN Country Team report PDF was too large for the web reader, and a UNDP water-conflict story repeatedly timed out; their indexed text was not used.
A 2024 UNDP land-degradation report was excluded because its publisher notice requires prior permission to reproduce material.
The local climate-security fieldwork in the inspected full report is from 2023–2024; no newer directly read field study was found here. Project-feature claims are not independent impact estimates.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
